headline: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases
pages: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has topped 12,000 confirmed cases, the country's Ministry of Health reported Thursday. Of the 12,021 confirmed cases, nearly half of the patients have died. It is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history and the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks. The outbreak, declared in May, is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which no vaccine or treatment is approved. Fighting between the army and rebels resumed Thursday in Iga-Barriere, north of Bunia, sending displaced people toward the city, a hub for the response. The World Health Organization said earlier fighting blocked teams from some communities and left some treatment centers short of staff.

About a dozen people, including two WHO staff, were evacuated after three days trapped in a hospital in Akwe. The outbreak is on track to pass the West African toll of 11,000 deaths from 2014 to 2016. Source: NPR.
